situation: You missed an important class last week because you were sick. You want to catch up on what you missed.
tasks: Explain why you missed the class.
Ask what material was covered.
Ask if you can meet during office hours.

situation: You borrowed a book from a classmate, but you accidentally spilled coffee on it.
tasks: Apologize for what happened.
Describe the damage.
Offer a way to fix the problem.

situation: Your campus gym has changed its opening hours, and now it closes before you finish class.
tasks: Explain your problem with the new hours.
Describe how this affects other students.
Suggest a solution.

situation: You want to join a volunteer program at a local animal shelter during the summer.
tasks: Introduce yourself.
Explain why you want to volunteer.
Ask about the schedule and requirements.

situation: Your roommate often plays loud music late at night, and you have trouble sleeping before exams.
tasks: Describe the problem politely.
Explain why it is important to you now.
Suggest a fair compromise.

situation: You ordered a textbook online for your course, but you received the wrong edition.
tasks: Describe your order and the problem.
Explain why you need the correct edition soon.
Ask for a replacement or a refund.

situation: You are organizing a study group for the final exam and want to invite a classmate you don't know well.
tasks: Introduce the study group.
Explain how it could help her.
Give details about the first meeting.

situation: The heating in your dormitory room has not worked for three days.
tasks: Describe the problem.
Explain how it is affecting you.
Ask when it will be repaired.

situation: Your professor gave you a lower grade than you expected on an essay, and you don't understand why.
tasks: Explain that you would like to understand the grade.
Ask about one specific comment.
Ask how you can improve your next essay.

situation: A friend from another country is going to visit you next month and has asked for advice.
tasks: Suggest the best way to travel to your city.
Recommend two places to visit.
Tell him what the weather will probably be like.

situation: You would like to change from one section of a course to another because of a schedule conflict.
tasks: Explain the schedule conflict.
Say which section you would like to join.
Ask what you need to do next.

situation: You attended a workshop on public speaking at the career center, and it was very helpful.
tasks: Thank her for the workshop.
Describe what you found most useful.
Suggest a topic for a future workshop.

situation: Your group project partner has not answered your messages for a week, and the deadline is close.
tasks: Remind him of the deadline.
Explain what still needs to be done.
Propose a time to meet.

situation: You found a wallet in the library and want to return it to its owner. There is a student card inside.
to: The student whose name is on the card, Mia
tasks: Explain what you found and where.
Describe how she can get it back.
Suggest a time and place to meet.

situation: The university cafeteria has very few healthy food options.
tasks: Describe the current situation.
Explain why healthy options are important to students.
Suggest two specific changes.

situation: You want to take a class that is already full, but it is required for your major.
tasks: Explain your situation.
Explain why you need the class this term.
Ask if there is any way to join.

situation: You are planning a surprise birthday party for a friend and want another friend's help.
tasks: Explain your plan.
Ask her to help with one specific task.
Tell her how to keep it a secret.

situation: You applied for a part-time job at the campus library but have not heard back after two weeks.
tasks: Remind them of your application.
Briefly repeat why you are a good candidate.
Ask about the status of your application.

situation: Your neighbor's dog barks for hours when the owner is not at home.
tasks: Describe the problem politely.
Explain how it affects you.
Suggest a possible solution.

situation: You lost your notes for an important course and want to borrow a classmate's notes.
tasks: Explain what happened.
Ask to borrow his notes.
Offer something in return.

situation: You want to start a new student club on campus about a hobby you enjoy.
tasks: Describe the club you want to start.
Explain why students would be interested.
Ask what steps you need to follow.

situation: Your internship supervisor asked you to work on a weekend, but you have an exam on Monday.
tasks: Explain your situation.
Offer an alternative time to work.
Thank her for understanding.

situation: The bus that goes to campus is often late, and many students arrive late to morning classes.
tasks: Describe the problem.
Explain how it affects students.
Suggest an improvement.

situation: A guest speaker gave a talk in your class about climate change, and you want to learn more.
tasks: Thank her for the talk.
Mention one idea that interested you.
Ask where you can find more information.

situation: You are going to be away for two weeks and need someone to take care of your plants.
tasks: Explain why you will be away.
Ask him to look after your plants.
Give simple instructions.

situation: You bought a used bicycle from a student, but the brakes do not work properly.
to: The student who sold it, Jordan
tasks: Describe the problem.
Remind him what he told you when you bought it.
Ask him to help solve the problem.

situation: Your English teacher recommended a book, and you enjoyed it very much.
tasks: Thank her for the recommendation.
Explain what you liked about the book.
Ask for another recommendation.

situation: You want to apply for a scholarship and need a reference letter from a teacher.
tasks: Explain what the scholarship is for.
Ask if she would write a reference letter.
Tell her the deadline.

situation: The Wi-Fi in the student residence is very slow in the evenings.
tasks: Describe the problem.
Explain when it usually happens.
Ask if they can improve the service.

situation: You and some classmates want to organize a trip to a science museum.
tasks: Describe the idea.
Explain how it is connected to the course.
Ask for his permission and support.

situation: A company you are interested in is holding an information session, but you cannot attend.
tasks: Explain why you cannot attend.
Express your interest in the company.
Ask if the session will be recorded.

situation: You received an invitation to a friend's wedding, but you have an important exam that week.
tasks: Thank her for the invitation.
Explain why you might not be able to come.
Suggest another way to celebrate with her.

situation: The campus library has decided to close its study rooms during the evening.
tasks: Explain why students use the study rooms in the evening.
Describe the effect of the change.
Ask the director to reconsider.

situation: You want to learn to play an instrument and found an advertisement for lessons.
tasks: Explain your experience with music.
Ask about prices and times.
Ask what you need to bring to the first lesson.

situation: A classmate helped you a lot with a difficult math assignment.
tasks: Thank her for her help.
Explain how the help made a difference.
Offer to help her in return.

situation: You are moving out of your apartment and want your security deposit returned.
tasks: Tell her the date you are moving out.
Describe the condition of the apartment.
Ask how and when the deposit will be returned.

situation: You want to take an online course during the summer, but you are not sure if the credits will count.
tasks: Describe the course you want to take.
Ask if the credits will transfer.
Ask what documents you need.

situation: Your class is collecting ideas for an end-of-year event.
tasks: Suggest an idea for the event.
Explain why your classmates would enjoy it.
Offer to help organize it.

situation: You noticed that the recycling bins in your building are always full and often overflow.
tasks: Describe the problem.
Explain why it is a concern.
Suggest how it could be solved.

situation: You were chosen to give a short presentation at a student conference but feel nervous.
tasks: Share the good news.
Explain what you are worried about.
Ask for advice on preparing.

situation: You want to rent a room in a shared house that you saw advertised online.
to: The owner of the house, Mr. Green
tasks: Introduce yourself.
Ask two questions about the room.
Ask when you could visit.

situation: Your professor posted the wrong date for the final exam on the course website.
tasks: Point out the mistake politely.
Explain why it is important to correct it.
Ask for the correct date.

situation: You enjoyed a local festival and want to volunteer to help next year.
tasks: Describe what you enjoyed.
Explain what skills you could offer.
Ask how to sign up.

situation: Your laptop broke and you need to use a computer to finish an assignment.
tasks: Explain what happened.
Ask for a short extension.
Explain how you will finish the work.

situation: A new student has joined your class and seems lonely.
tasks: Welcome her to the class.
Invite her to an activity.
Offer to help her with anything she needs.

situation: You would like to write an article for the student newspaper.
tasks: Introduce yourself.
Describe your article idea.
Ask about the word limit and deadline.

situation: The campus parking fees have increased a lot this year.
tasks: Describe the change.
Explain how it affects students.
Suggest an alternative.

situation: You forgot to return a library book and received a large fine.
tasks: Explain why the book was late.
Ask if the fine can be reduced.
Promise to be more careful in the future.

situation: Your cousin is deciding which university to attend and asked about yours.
tasks: Describe what you like about your university.
Mention one disadvantage.
Give her one piece of advice.

situation: You want to ask a former teacher for advice about choosing a career.
tasks: Remind him who you are.
Explain the career choice you are considering.
Ask for his advice.
